releases.body: This release retunes brainstorming after its rebuild in v7.0.0. Many of you told us, rightly, that the new default questions got annoying fast and felt formulaic. Brainstorming now digs for context before it asks anything, and tries to ask better questions. We expect to keep tuning it, but we think it's better than it was. It also trims three long skills so they better survive compaction on Claude Code, and changes the issue and PR templates to ask for a summary written by a human. ### Brainstorming - **It digs for context first.** In an existing project, or when you point it at a spec, plan, or files, it reads them before its first message and doesn't ask what they already answer. (#2560) - **It tries to ask better questions.** v7.0.0 opened every session the same way: an offer to skip th

We rebuilt brainstorming from scratch so it does a much better job of what it was always for: helping you work out what you actually want and put it into words before anything gets built. The new skill asks you to describe what you're after and why, plays back what it heard so you can correct it, and keeps asking good questions until the picture is clear. Then it matches the process to the work, from just doing it to writing a full design. This release also adds a native plugin manifest for the Antigravity Marketplace and fixes Windows hook discovery, Git Bash paths, Hermes skill descriptions, and several smaller bugs. ### Brainstorming - **Brainstorming draws out what you want before it proposes anything.** Its first message offers to skip the questions and asks one open question about a

`writing-plans` produces leaner plans, faster. Plans now record the decisions an implementer needs (signatures, test assertions, the spec's values) instead of writing out the code. Some frontier models, including Opus 5.5, could get overzealous during plan writing and, with certain prompting, would sometimes try to implement the entire project while designing the plan. The new skill keeps planning focused on the plan. When we reproduced the original report, the scratch builds went away, and plans took a quarter of the time and about a third of the tokens. Thanks to Harper Reed for the report and session bundle. (#2333) ### Writing Plans - **A plan records decisions. It's not a transcript of the code.** "What a Step Contains" replaces the "No Placeholders" section. A test step names the tes

releases.body: - Starting a session that already has a run in progress now reattaches to the live session instead of replacing its runtime. Before, the original run kept going but couldn't be reached, and its transcript writes landed on a stale snapshot. A start that includes a prompt while a run is in progress is rejected - The hub records every client that registered a capability for a session, including clients that join a task that's already running, and sends each request to the first one still connected. If none is left, the request fails quickly with a message the user can act on, instead of waiting forever - A turn whose connection drops after the model has streamed only reasoning is now retried, and the partial reasoning is discarded. Turns with text, media or tool calls are still never retried

- A new **Changes** button in the session header shows the session's line counts and opens a pane listing the files changed in the last turn or across the whole session, with a diff of each. When a turn finishes, a summary under it lists the files it changed; click it to open the pane on that turn - A **project files panel** (folder button in the session header) shows a file tree beside the conversation, with a read-only tabbed viewer, git status letters, and a marker on files the session changed. Files the agent edited get a File/Diff toggle. Works on local and SSH environments - An integrated **terminal panel** opens at the bottom of the window (toggle with Ctrl+backtick) - Pull request status moved from the bar above the composer into a header button. Its menu shows the PR title, merge

- Opening a task that's already running in another Cline app now attaches to that run instead of starting a second one that couldn't be stopped. If an app closes mid-task, requests waiting on it now fail with a clear message instead of hanging - `cline hub status` and `cline doctor` no longer hang on a Hub that has frozen. Its health check now times out after 3s and the Hub is reported as not running - A turn whose connection drops after the model has streamed only reasoning (for example, "The socket connection was closed unexpectedly") is now retried instead of ending the run - Model requests retry at most 3 times instead of 5 - Kimi K3 now gets `max` reasoning for Extra High and Max, instead of an `xhigh` setting it rejects - Gemini API keys (the `gemini` provider) no longer send native

## Speech Ollama can now generate [speech](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/speech) on macOS. `ollama run` plays text or a chat model's reply aloud as the audio is generated, and apps can stream audio through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/audio/speech` endpoint. ```sh ollama run phonon "Hello from Ollama." ``` ## d3 decision models [d3](https://ollama.com/library/d3) brings vLLM Semantic Router's decision models to Ollama. Give a model text, structured state, or an image, and ask it to classify, answer yes or no, or score options with probabilities. The family includes 2B, 4B, 9B, and 27B sizes. ```sh ollama run d3 "A customer says their card was charged twice." --ask "Is this a billing issue?" ``` ## New Contributors * @SynapShift made their first contribution in https://github.com/ollam

releases.body: # Axolotl v0.21.0 Release Notes 59 commits since v0.20.0 (September 30, 2026). This release is headlined by Reflection's Beam, a 501B-parameter MoE you can QLoRA-tune on a single node. We also added native diffusion language model training, image datasets for DPO, KTO, and GRPO, and optimizations for the training loop. --- ## Highlights ### **Reflection Beam** You can now fine-tune Reflection's Beam, a 501B-parameter MoE with 23B active parameters, using QLoRA on a single 8xH200 node. QLoRA configs ship for FSDP2 and `device_map`, plus expert-parallel LoRA recipes for B200 in bf16, NVFP4, and NF4. [Get started with the Beam guide](https://docs.axolotl.ai/docs/models/beam.html). - Contributed by @HamidShojanazeri and @winglian in #4148, and @NanoCode012 in #4163. ### **Native Diffusion LM T

# Axolotl v0.20.0 Release Notes There has been 67 commits since v0.19.0 (September 10, 2026). We have added a bunch of features including GGUF export, Ringmaster context parallelism, native NVFP4 LoRA, and expert parallelism without DeepEP. Python 3.12 and torch 2.13.0 are now the minimums, and FSDP1 is removed. --- ## Highlights ### **GGUF Export** You can now convert a trained checkpoint to GGUF for llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, and llamafile with `axolotl export config.yml --quantize Q4_K_M,Q8_0`, which emits the base conversion plus one file per requested quant type. [See the guide](https://docs.axolotl.ai/docs/export.html). - Contributed by @ved1beta in #3950. ### **Context Parallelism with Ringmaster** You can now train long-context runs with packed sequences under Ulysses, Ring, or

# Axolotl v0.19.0 Release Notes 72 commits since v0.18.0 (July 17, 2026). We have a variety of changes this release including a new declarative model-support system, seven new model families plus ternary (BitNet b1.58) QAT, two new optimizers, a big chat-template tokenization speedup, and PyTorch 2.13 support. --- ## Highlights ### **Declarative Model Support Profiles** Adding a new architecture used to mean edits scattered across the loaders. A model now picks a family template (`VANILLA_CAUSAL_LM`, `IMAGE_TEXT_TO_TEXT`) and declares only what makes it different. Existing descriptors keep working, and there are no config changes. [See the guide](https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/blob/main/docs/agents/new_model_support.md). - Contributed by @thad0ctor in #3869 and @winglian in #3

## Features ### 🛠️ TRL now trains on AWS Trainium The fused LM head from v1.15 is what made Neuron tractable; the remaining gaps are closed here. There is a [guide](https://huggingface.co/docs/trl/neuron) to go with it. Neuron recompiles once per input shape, so an unpadded run stalls about a minute on every new sequence length. `pad_to_multiple_of` now defaults to `"auto"`: 128 on Neuron, `None` elsewhere, so nothing changes on GPU. Trainium2, Qwen3-0.6B SFT, 20 steps: **130 s with the default against 260 s without**. * Add a guide for training on AWS Trainium by @qgallouedec in https://github.com/huggingface/trl/pull/7729 *

## Features ### ⚡ Fused LM head: up to 6.9× longer sequences on the same GPU SFT, DPO, KTO, GRPO, RLOO and Distillation now score tokens with a **fused LM head**: a Triton kernel projects the hidden states through the LM head in tiles and reduces to per-token log-probs and entropy directly, so the `[batch, seq, vocab]` logits tensor is never built. It is **on by default**, there is nothing to turn on. **Max trainable sequence length** (gemma-3-1b, 262k vocabulary, 79 GiB of GPU memory, bf16, batch size 1, gradient checkpointing, sdpa): | Trainer | v1.14.2 | v1.15.0 | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | DPO | 10,240 | **59,392** | **5.80×** |

Patch release fixing two cases of silently wrong training and three crashes. Worth calling out: **#7505** affects GRPO, RLOO and Distillation on the default generation path (`use_vllm=False`). Models that end a turn with an id only their generation config declares (Gemma 3/4, Phi-3.5, ...) did not stop at the end of the turn, and everything generated after it was trained on, up to `max_completion_length`. The only visible sign was `completions/clipped_ratio` close to 1. With vLLM, generation stopped correctly but the metrics were still wrong, and `mask_truncated_completions=True` dropped every finished completion. Runs on models whose tokenizer eos is their only end-of-turn id are unchanged. ## What's Changed * Keep the DFT loss finite on a batch with no trainable tokens by @albertvillanov
